entry.title: [HIGH] Explicit PreToolUse `defer` decisions can dead-end tool calls.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code hook setup found that a `PreToolUse` hook returning `hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision: "defer"` is not equivalent to a silent pass-through. Matching tool calls can stop at `tool_deferred`, receive a synthetic missing-tool-result error on a later continuation path, or leave subagent Bash calls without any `tool_result` while the parent sees a completed-looking task. Comments reproduced the issue in the CLI and TypeScript Agent SDK, including cases where a fast synchronous `defer` raced the assistant stream closure and produced `[Tool result missing due to internal error]` instead of a clean suspended call.

entry.title: [HIGH] Non-interactive permission denials can block the grant path
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code desktop/web non-interactive session denied an infrastructure CLI command in auto permission mode, then also denied the documented settings-editing path that would have added the needed allow rule. Because `/permissions` was unavailable on that surface, the user had no in-session prompt or approval UI to raise the authorization ceiling; a direct edit to `.claude/settings.local.json` succeeded, leaving the sanctioned config-update path stricter than raw file editing.

entry.title: [HIGH] TUI Markdown rendering can renumber non-sequential list references.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.234 Linux TUI repro shows assistant output containing intentionally non-sequential ordered-list markers, such as 1, 5, 6, and 8, rendered back to the user as 1, 2, 3, and 4. The raw conversation JSON preserved the literal numbers, but the TUI applied normal Markdown ordered-list normalization, making cross-references appear to point at different source items and causing the assistant to deny a rendered item number the user could see. This is a semantic display corruption rather than a model-only mistake because the transcript and the terminal view disagree.

entry.title: [MEDIUM] VS Code extension can reject `/mcp reconnect <server>` with a terminal-readiness error.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code VS Code native extension repro found that running `/mcp reconnect <server-name>` fails even when the integrated terminal is idle and no permission dialog, overlay, or streaming turn is active. The bare `/mcp` command still works and prints usage that includes the reconnect argument form, but the named reconnect command returns a CLI/TUI-style readiness message about the terminal still starting up or showing another view. In the VS Code chat sidebar that condition does not map cleanly to the UI, so the command appears to be unavailable or guarded by the wrong readiness check.

entry.title: [HIGH] Auto mode Bash edits can escape /rewind checkpoints.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.234 WSL2 repro found that, when auto mode is active, the built-in prompt can steer the model to make file changes through Bash tools such as Python heredocs, sed, or redirected shell writes instead of the dedicated Edit or Write tools. Those Bash-authored writes were not tracked by the checkpoint system, so /rewind reported success while leaving modified and newly created files on disk. The mismatch is silent unless the user manually checks git status, and later turns can build on code the user believed had been reverted.

entry.title: [HIGH] Project-scoped autoMode config can be silently ignored.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.233 repro found that an `autoMode` block placed in project `.claude/settings.json` or `.claude/settings.local.json` is ignored by design, but the shipped JSON schema does not mark `autoMode` as user-, managed-, or flag-scope only while sibling restricted keys do. The documented verification command, `claude auto-mode config`, then prints a default-looking effective config with no warning, and `claude doctor`, interactive startup, headless startup, and explicit `--setting-sources project` also give no signal that the project-scope block was discarded. A one-character path mistake between `.claude/settings.json` and `~/.claude/settings.json` can therefore drop custom auto-mode classifier rules silently.

entry.title: [HIGH] Headless startup can replace invalid ~/.claude.json with defaults.
entry.summary: A reproduced Claude Code report shows that adding invalid JSON syntax, such as a C-style comment, to a working `~/.claude.json` has different recovery behavior by entrypoint. Interactive `claude` stops at a configuration-error screen and leaves the file untouched, but a non-interactive launch such as `claude -p "hi"` reports the configuration file as corrupted and rewrites the live file with defaults. That removes saved `mcpServers` and other settings from the active config, even though a timestamped backup is created under `~/.claude/backups/`. The JSON parse failure is expected because `~/.claude.json` is strict JSON; the limitation is that the headless recovery path mutates live configuration instead of failing closed.

entry.title: [HIGH] Windows/WSL shared repos can make live worktrees look prunable.
entry.summary: A reported Windows 11 plus WSL2 setup used one NTFS repository from both native Windows paths and /mnt/c WSL paths. Git worktree registrations written by one side stored absolute gitdir paths in that side's spelling, so the other side could not stat them and reported the still-live worktrees as prunable. Claude Code automatic worktree cleanup then deleted the other side's .git/worktrees registrations during session startup, breaking active sessions and making later git commands fail with not-a-git-repository errors. In the report, a failed git show redirection also truncated a working file to zero bytes after the registration vanished.

entry.title: [HIGH] macOS Desktop can split or freeze transcripts for Unicode-normalized project paths
entry.summary: On macOS, Claude Desktop's resume migration can slugify a project path from decomposed Unicode bytes while the CLI writes transcripts under the NFC-normalized slug. For projects whose path contains combining marks or accented folder names, Desktop can copy or move a transcript into a second project directory, pin its UI to a frozen snapshot, and hide later CLI-written turns after restart or idle resume. In the reported 1.30096.1 through 1.32352.1 repro, Desktop logs showed transcript migration from the NFC slug to an NFD-derived slug, and the NFD-side file remained only a byte-prefix of the current NFC transcript.

entry.title: [HIGH] Windows Desktop cross-session send_message can ghost-deliver without enqueueing.
entry.summary: A reported Windows 11 Claude Desktop setup found that cross-session `send_message` between local sessions could return success and render the message in the target session UI while never appending it to the target session's real `.jsonl` transcript and never delivering it to the model. The reporter checked unique markers across multiple sends, saw the target transcript mtime remain frozen, and found the ghost messages disappeared after app restart. The receiving session could also enter phantom-running states with a spinner, frozen activity timestamps, and no persisted user turn.

entry.title: [MEDIUM] Cloud sessions can drop project-declared plugin marketplaces while reading enabledPlugins.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.234 cloud-session repro found that project `.claude/settings.json` could read an `enabledPlugins` entry for a GitHub marketplace plugin while dropping the same file's `extraKnownMarketplaces` declaration. Startup logs then reported the enabled plugin as orphaned because the marketplace was not registered, saved zero installed plugins, and later said `installPluginsForHeadless: no marketplaces declared`. The public cloud and desktop docs pointed users at repo-declared plugins as the cloud-session path, while a shipped guard and a follow-up static read of the binary suggested project-scope marketplaces are excluded from the declared-marketplace map.

entry.title: [HIGH] WebFetch can report live content for error pages in unattended routines.
entry.summary: A reported Claude cloud Scheduled Task used WebFetch to verify a job URL and emailed the result as a live listing, but a real browser showed the URL was a bare 500 Internal Server Error page. Follow-up WebFetch calls over more than 15 minutes still returned a detailed job posting, including under prompts asking for raw page text and explicitly forbidding fabrication. The user later supplied raw HTML showing only the 500 error page, so the agent-visible tool result did not match the current browser-visible source. The report does not prove whether the cause is stale cache, backend fetch behavior, or summarization fabrication.

entry.title: [HIGH] CLAUDE.md rules can be recitable but not enforced on late shared-resource edits.
entry.summary: A reported long Claude Code session against a shared Figma document had explicit user-level CLAUDE.md rules requiring a fresh refetch before editing shared resources. Late in the session, after the human edited the same Figma text node outside Claude, Claude corrected one factual error by rewriting the whole node from an earlier in-context copy instead of refetching current state. The human's concurrent edit was silently destroyed and was not recoverable from Figma autosave. Afterward, Claude could quote the relevant CLAUDE.md rules back correctly, so the failure was not simply a missing memory-file load.

entry.title: [HIGH] MCP secret env values can be redacted before reaching the subprocess.
entry.summary: A reported Windows 11 Claude Code Desktop setup configured an MCP server with an env block referencing `GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN` through `${GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN}`. The server then failed because the value delivered to the child process contained U+2022 redaction characters, producing `Cannot convert argument to a ByteString because the character at index 15 has a value of 8226`. The reporter reproduced after setting the variable through `setx`, fully restarting Claude Code, and rebooting, including an attempt where the token was typed into a fresh PowerShell window and never appeared in the chat transcript.

entry.title: [MEDIUM] CLAUDE.md symlinked to AGENTS.md refuses direct tool writes.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code setup followed the documented `CLAUDE.md -> AGENTS.md` symlink pattern, then found that Read succeeds while Edit and Write on `CLAUDE.md` fail with `Refusing to write through symlink`. A maintainer reproduced the behavior on released 2.1.234 and clarified that refusing symlink writes is an intentional safety guard, but that the memory docs do not warn users that the documented symlink form cannot be directly updated by Claude Code's file-writing tools.

entry.title: [HIGH] MCP permission approval can return without unblocking the tool call.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.233 macOS session showed MCP tools from a connected server returning `MCP tool call requires approval` even after the user tapped `Allow once` in the client permission prompt. The prompt rendered normally and produced no visible error, but retrying the same `add_repo` and `get_session` calls on the same server produced the identical approval-required response across multiple attempts and after reopening the app. The result is an approval UI that appears accepted while the underlying MCP tool state remains blocked.

entry.title: [MEDIUM] Editing settings.json hook commands can fail false JSON validation.
entry.summary: A reported Windows 11 Git Bash setup found that the Claude Code Edit tool repeatedly refused an otherwise valid `.claude/settings.json` change when the edited hook `command` string contained shell regex metacharacters such as `'.ts$'`. The tool reported `Invalid JSON: JSON Parse error: Unterminated string` and rolled the edit back, while independent `jq` validation passed before and after, and writing the same value through a structured JSON mutation succeeded immediately. The failure appears to be in the Edit tool's settings validator or patch path, not in the final JSON bytes.

entry.title: [HIGH] CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR can name a different account than the session appears to spend.
entry.summary: A reported Windows Claude Code Desktop and CLI setup with several config roots found that a desktop-launched session exposed `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `claude auth status`, and model-visible context for one account while desktop session records, usage samples, and owner confirmation indicated another account was being billed. Follow-up measurements found contradictory account identifiers inside the same config file, including an OAuth identity for one account and cached usage for another. The reporter explicitly notes that the signing credential was not directly measured, so the hard limitation is that local tooling cannot reliably identify the effective account or billing boundary from the available session surfaces.

entry.title: [HIGH] Bash tool timeouts can background commands instead of cancelling them.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.233 Linux repro found that a Bash tool call with a 3s timeout returned control to the agent while the underlying process continued running for roughly 16 more seconds. The reporter tied the behavior to multi-hour VM disk-saturation incidents under concurrent subagent load, where many individually timed-out commands could continue consuming I/O after the tool layer appeared to have moved on.

entry.title: [MEDIUM] Resume picker search can miss retained sessions outside the 50 most recent.
entry.summary: A reported Linux Claude Code 2.1.233 repro found that both the in-session `/resume` picker and standalone `claude --resume` picker load only the 50 most recent sessions, and the type-to-search filter searches only that loaded subset rather than all retained transcript files on disk. A month-old session whose generated title contained the search term was not findable until its transcript file mtime was moved back into the top 50. This means a high `cleanupPeriodDays` setting can retain old transcripts without making them discoverable in the UI.
